Marissa / team  see my quick unit-econ sketch below (attached as unit-econ-model.xlsx). High-level recommendations that map to FintechX constraints: 

Assumptions (baseline / expected):
- Pilot volume: 30M tokens/mo. Scale target: 150M tokens/mo.
- Average token length per feature call: 750 tokens (summary + context).
- Operational overhead + egress: +8% on top of token compute.

Redwood cost model (net to us after infra optimizations):
- Conservative: $120 / 1M tokens
- Expected: $70 / 1M tokens
- Aggressive (with quant + cache): $40 / 1M tokens

Pricing recommendations (map to FintechX target margin >=50%):
- To meet >=50% gross margin at 30M/mo, list price needs to be roughly 2x cost:
  - If cost $70/1M -> list $140/1M (gives ~50% margin)
  - If cost $40/1M -> list $80/1M (comfortably >50% margin)

Per-feature mapping example (summary feature):
- If average user triggers 4 summary calls / month at 0.75k tokens each -> ~3k tokens/user/mo.
- At list $140/1M -> feature unit price ~ $0.42 / MAU/month.
- At list $80/1M -> feature unit price ~ $0.24 / MAU/month.

CAC payback & target:
- FintechX target <=9 months; ideal 6 months. With feature-level ARPU uplift of $2 4/mo per acquired user, and assuming CAC of $40 $60, payback is ~10 20 months unless we price the feature to secure higher ARPU or reduce CAC.
- Recommendation: pilot discount to accelerate adoption (50% off list for first 3 months) and joint case study to reduce CAC.

Pilot terms suggestion: 3 months, up to 50M tokens total, discounted price at expected tier ($70/1M net -> offer $35/1M net to FintechX) with overage at expected list rate. SLA and basic security posture as discussed.

I attached a model with sensitivity tables (unit-econ-model.xlsx)  happy to walk through on the follow-up.
